CLINICAL HISTORY: 47-year-old presenting with unexplained weight loss and fatigue of three weeks duration. Referred from the emergency department for further characterisation. Relevant past history includes no significant comorbidity.

TECHNIQUE: CT of the chest and abdomen performed on a 64-slice scanner. Intravenous contrast was administered in arterial and portal venous phases. Reconstructions were obtained in the axial, coronal and sagittal planes at 2.0 mm slice thickness. Image quality was diagnostic.

COMPARISON: Prior CT of the abdomen and pelvis of 11 January, and the corresponding report, were available for direct comparison. Where measurements are given below they have been made on comparable sequences at the same anatomical level.

BOWEL AND PERITONEUM: The stomach and small bowel are non-dilated. No free intraperitoneal gas or fluid. The appendix is not confidently identified; there is no periappendiceal inflammatory change. Colonic diverticulosis is noted in the sigmoid without evidence of acute diverticulitis.

LIVER AND BILIARY: The liver measures 14.1 cm in craniocaudal extent and is homogeneous in attenuation. A 8 mm hypodense lesion is noted in segment VI, unchanged from the prior study. The gallbladder is distended without wall thickening or pericholecystic fluid. The intra- and extrahepatic bile ducts are not dilated.

MEDIASTINUM: The heart is normal in size. No pericardial effusion. Mediastinal lymph nodes measure up to 11 mm in the short axis, within normal limits for size. The thoracic aorta is of normal calibre without dissection or aneurysm. The oesophagus is unremarkable where visualised.

MUSCULOSKELETAL: Degenerative change is present in the lumbar spine with anterior osteophytes and facet hypertrophy. No aggressive or lytic bone lesion. No acute fracture. Muscle bulk and fat planes are preserved.

PANCREAS, SPLEEN AND ADRENALS: The pancreas is normal in size and contour without ductal dilatation or peripancreatic stranding. The spleen measures 10.4 cm and is homogeneous. Both adrenal glands are normal in thickness without discrete nodule.

KIDNEYS AND URINARY TRACT: Both kidneys enhance symmetrically. A 22 mm simple cortical cyst is present in the right kidney, of no clinical significance. No hydronephrosis, calculus or perinephric stranding. The ureters are not dilated. The bladder is partially distended with a smooth wall.

MEASURABLE DISEASE: Lesions are numbered consistently with the prior report where correspondence could be established.
  1. Lesion in the left external iliac chain, measuring 33 mm in the greatest axial dimension (newly apparent since the prior study). Margins are ill defined; attenuation is peripherally enhancing.
  2. Lesion in the retroperitoneum, para-aortic station, measuring 24 mm in the greatest axial dimension (newly apparent since the prior study). Margins are ill defined; attenuation is heterogeneous with central necrosis.
  3. Lesion in the left supraclavicular fossa, measuring 20 mm in the greatest axial dimension (previously 35 mm, stable within measurement error). Margins are lobulated; attenuation is peripherally enhancing.
  4. Lesion in the porta hepatis, measuring 59 mm in the greatest axial dimension (previously 45 mm, representing interval increase). Margins are well defined; attenuation is homogeneous.
  5. Lesion in the TIV vertebral body, measuring 76 mm in the greatest axial dimension (previously 92 mm, representing interval increase). Margins are lobulated; attenuation is peripherally enhancing.
  6. Lesion in the porta hepatis, measuring 20 mm in the greatest axial dimension (previously 24 mm, representing interval increase). Margins are ill defined; attenuation is homogeneous.
  7. Lesion in the right hepatic lobe, segment II, measuring 62 mm in the greatest axial dimension (previously 46 mm, representing interval increase). Margins are ill defined; attenuation is homogeneous.
  8. Lesion in the gastrohepatic ligament, measuring 81 mm in the greatest axial dimension (unchanged from the prior study). Margins are spiculated; attenuation is peripherally enhancing.
  9. Lesion in the left hepatic lobe, segment III, measuring 52 mm in the greatest axial dimension (previously 60 mm, representing interval increase). Margins are ill defined; attenuation is peripherally enhancing.
  10. Lesion in the right hepatic lobe, segment III, measuring 40 mm in the greatest axial dimension (previously 55 mm, stable within measurement error). Margins are well defined; attenuation is homogeneous.
  11. Lesion in the left adrenal gland, measuring 78 mm in the greatest axial dimension (previously 94 mm, stable within measurement error). Margins are spiculated; attenuation is heterogeneous with central necrosis.
  12. Lesion in the left supraclavicular fossa, measuring 34 mm in the greatest axial dimension (newly apparent since the prior study). Margins are ill defined; attenuation is homogeneous.
  13. Lesion in the right hepatic lobe, segment 11, measuring 76 mm in the greatest axial dimension (previously 85 mm, representing interval decrease). Margins are well defined; attenuation is peripherally enhancing.
  14. Lesion in the retroperitoneum, para-aortic station, measuring 76 mm in the greatest axial dimension (previously 67 mm, representing interval decrease). Margins are lobulated; attenuation is heterogeneous with central necrosis.
  15. Lesion in the porta hepatis, measuring 78 mm in the greatest axial dimension (previously 73 mm, representing interval increase). Margins are ill defined; attenuation is peripherally enhancing.
  16. Lesion in the spleen, upper pole, measuring 51 mm in the greatest axial dimension (previously 71 mm, representing interval increase). Margins are well defined; attenuation is heterogeneous with central necrosis.
  17. Lesion in the right hepatic lobe, segment VIII, measuring 32 mm in the greatest axial dimension (newly apparent since the prior study). Margins are well defined; attenuation is peripherally enhancing.
  18. Lesion in the left hepatic lobe, segment IV, measuring 83 mm in the greatest axial dimension (previously 103 mm, stable within measurement error). Margins are ill defined; attenuation is peripherally enhancing.
  19. Lesion in the left adrenal gland, measuring 27 mm in the greatest axial dimension (newly apparent since the prior study). Margins are ill defined; attenuation is peripherally enhancing.

IMPRESSION: 1. Interval resolution of the previously described inflammatory change. 2. Colonic diverticulosis without acute inflammation. 3. No acute finding requiring immediate intervention.

RECOMMENDATION: Correlation with laboratory results is advised. These findings were discussed with the referring clinician at the time of reporting.
